fields.statement: Plan review round 3 left finding f1 (contradiction on scaled-test-clock-env): The 1 ms Sleep floor plus the real-time timeout floor turns the scripts' own short waits into near-busy loops, which contradicts the scaled-test-clock Decision (no busy loop on the shared 4-core VM; polls keep their count). 42 wait steps across about 35 scripts in cmd/rhiza/testdata/script use timeout = "30s" with interval = "50ms" (e.g. until = "test -f ../go", a shell spawned per poll). At scale 1000 each 50 ms sleep is cut to the 1 ms floor, so the 30 s virtual deadline passes after about 600 condition spawns. Then, inside the 3 s real floor, engine.go wait() sleeps 'its interval' (1 ms again): up to about 3000 more spawns, against about 60 per 3 s today. The same steps' real budget for background work also drops from 30 s to 3 s. The plan neither bounds the poll rate inside the floor (e.g. a real-time minimum per poll) nor accounts for these scripts. The critic confirmed it: Verified: 43 kind="wait" steps in cmd/rhiza/testdata/script use timeout = "30s" with interval = "50ms" (29 until = "test -f ../go", the rest rhiza ship check), each condition a spawned process. engine.go wait() (902-957) sleeps c.Sleep(min(sleep, timeout-elapsed)) each poll; under the leaf's clock Sleep(50ms) waits the 1 ms floor, so polls run ~50x as often as today (about 1000 spawns/s instead of 20), and the leaf's 'sleeps its interval' inside the real-time floor is again 1 ms. Nothing in the statement or acceptance bounds the real poll rate, and these steps' real budget for background work drops from 30 s to 3 s, a flake risk on the loaded shared VM. This contradicts the scaled-test-clock Decision's promise that polls keep their count at a thousandth of the cost and AGENTS.md's no-busy-loop rule; major stands. How should it be settled?

Plan review round 3 left finding f2 (missing-acceptance on scripts-run-on-scaled-clock): The failure case 'a script that clears it (env RHIZA_TEST_CLOCK_SCALE=) runs on RealClock, shown by a short wait-timeout script' does not say what the script asserts. Under the plan's own real-time floor (min(timeout, 3 s)), a short wait that times out takes the same wall time on the scaled clock as on RealClock, so a timing-based script cannot tell them apart. The acceptance must name an observable that differs, such as the condition's run count or the 'did not hold' detail after N checks. The critic confirmed it: Verified: no wait-timeout.txtar exists yet, and the leaf's failure case says only that the new script 'shows' RealClock. With the real-time floor min(timeout, 3 s), a short wait that times out takes the same wall time on both clocks, and wait()'s timeout detail ('did not hold within <timeout>[: last]') carries no poll count, so neither timing nor the timeout message tells the clocks apart. Without a named observable (condition run count, a 'held after N checks' detail) the point can be met by a vacuous script; an unverifiable acceptance point is missing-acceptance, major. How should it be settled?

Plan review round 3 left finding f3 (missing-acceptance on api-waits-on-run-clock): The statement moves ship_deploy.go's interval and deadline (today time.Now/time.Sleep, ship_deploy.go:85-99), run_spawn.go's spawnSleep (time.Sleep(spawnPoll) when ctx.Sleep is nil) and the default ctx.Sleep of retryGH (ship.go:610) and retryRex (session.go:892) onto the scaled clock. The acceptance checks only runClock's selection and typePointer: nothing runs to show that ship deploy measures its deadline on the same clock it sleeps on (the Decision scaled-clock-now-skips-sleeps names this case) or that the spawn poll and the retries use the scaled clock with the variable set and time.Sleep without it. The critic confirmed it: Verified: ship_deploy.go:85-99 measures its deadline with time.Now and sleeps time.Sleep(interval); run_spawn.go:253-258 falls back to time.Sleep(spawnPoll); the leaf's statement moves these and the retryGH/retryRex default sleeps onto the scaled clock. The acceptance runs only TestRunClock/TestTypePointer and the existing TestSessionMessage/TestRun: nothing shows ship deploy's deadline is measured on the clock it sleeps on (the case the scaled-clock-now-skips-sleeps Decision exists for: a scaled sleep against a wall deadline would hammer a real HTTP probe), nor that the spawn poll and the retries switch with the variable. Statement points with no acceptance; major stands. How should it be settled?
